notes.title: Strange Antiquities is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
Strange Antiquities is out now!
Our release has finally arrived: the doors to Strange Antiquities are now open!


You can watch our brand-new launch trailer below: 

[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/x5SmaoTT8r8"][/dynamiclink]

After several years of tinkering, puzzling, and more than a few nights spent burning the candle at both ends, we are thrilled to welcome you back to Undermere. If this is your first visit, don’t worry: no prior knowledge is required.

Step into your new role as apprentice Thaumaturge, running an occult curiosity shop that is cosy, mysterious, and full of secrets waiting to be discovered.

To celebrate our return to Undermere, we’re launching with a 10% discount for the first week.


Share your thoughts

We’re just two brothers making these strange little games, and your feedback means a lot to us.  If you’ve already spent some time in the shop, please consider leaving us a review! It’s one of the best ways to support small indie teams. Reviews not only help us understand how you’re finding the game, they also help new players to discover it.


Join the community

If you encounter any bugs or major hiccups, feel free to report them in our Steam Forums. If you want to swap notes with fellow Thaumaturges, share your theories, or just chat about how best to arrange your shelves, you can hop on the Iceberg Interactive Discord.


Thank You

It’s been a wonderful journey, and we want to thank you for your support. We’ve poured everything we have into Strange Antiquities, and seeing players step into the shop at last feels amazing.



The ravens are circling, Jupiter the cat is waiting for pets, and the bell won’t ding itself…


Welcome to Strange Antiquities.


Rob & John

notes.title: The Thaumaturge’s Handbook: An FAQ for Strange Antiquities
notes.content:
Dear Thaumaturges,



Before you set foot on the creaky floorboards of our shop on Hollowell Lane, we figured some of you still might have a few questions about your role, the shop, and the journey ahead. In this blog, we’ll answer a handful of them to make sure you don’t cause someone’s demise during your very first shift.


Do I need to have played Strange Horticulture?

No. Strange Antiquities is a stand-alone sequel set in the same world but tells a completely separate story. Returning players will find familiar mechanics and lore, but the game has been designed to be welcoming for new players too. Take your time - discovery is part of the experience. And if you’re ever stuck, there’s a hint button to help.


Will there be some familiar faces?

Yes. Previous visitors to Undermere may spot some familiar customers, along with crossover lore, references, and Easter Eggs for fans of Strange Horticulture.



Will there be multiple endings again?

Yes! There are at least 8 distinct endings to discover. None of them are “wrong” - they’re simply reflections of the path you took.



What about the Closer Inspect system?

We’ve expanded the “Closer Inspect” mechanic so you can now examine items in greater detail. There are four categories of analysis, and you can hover your mouse over different sections of each artefact to uncover useful information and hidden clues.



… and the new books?

You’ll find several new tomes to study, packed with hints and lore to help identify strange antiquities.



What else is new?

Err. No more spoilers now - you’ll have to play the game and discover the game’s secrets for yourself. 



I need to know: can you still pet the cat?

Of course. His name is Jupiter. To be honest, if regular petting is not part of your daily ritual, then one might infer that you’re a monster.



Eli White told me not to touch anything. I’m sure that means there are no secrets to discover, right?

Let's just say rules were meant to be broken... 😉 



What are the controls?

The game is fully playable with just a mouse.

Right-click to inspect.

Mouse wheel for magnifying glass. 


There are also keyboard shortcuts for those with a different play style.

Arrow keys/WASD to move around the shop.

Shift for magnifying glass



Is there controller support?

Yes.



Does it play well on Steam Deck?

Yes. Tested, tuned, and Verified on Steam Deck!



How long is the game?

Tricky to say. 6-10 hours, but possibly longer, depending on how you play. 



What is the price point?

$17.99 with a 10% launch discount



What engine does it run on?

Unity.



Do you plan to release it on additional platforms?

PC and Nintendo Switch at launch. More platforms to follow in due course.


What about Mac?

Mac is a priority for us, but we couldn’t get it ready in time for launch. Please bear with us - we’ll update you as soon as we can…



What are the accessibility options?

Easy-to-read fonts

Zoom with the Magnifying Glass 

“Closer Inspect” descriptions include colour cues - we’re colourblind ourselves, and we’ve tried to make sure fellow colour-impaired folk can play comfortably. 

Mouse-only controls, but with added keyboard support.

Arachnophia setting - there’s a small spider who sometimes wanders around the clock. His name is Tony. He’s harmless… but you can toggle him off if you’d prefer not to see him.



What languages is the game in?

At launch: English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Polish, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian.


I want to cover the game on my channel/blog/outlet. How do I get a key?

For any coverage inquiries, just send an email to pr\[at]iceberg-games\[dot]com! 



Where do I report bugs if I find one?

You can report any bugs and hiccups in our Steam forum. We’ll set up a dedicated bug-reproting thread here. 

I uncovered some haunted antiquities in my grandpa’s attic. What do I do?

Apprentice at Strange Antiquities, and you’ll soon learn that every object has its uses… and its dangers.

notes.title: Undermere Herald - June Edition | Performance Review & Gamescom News
notes.content:
Dear Thaumaturges,

We’d like to congratulate you on your great performance during your trial period. You’ve shown curiosity and thick skin, the qualities needed to run a shop like Strange Antiquities.  

Maybe we’ll call you up to run the shop shortly… 

We realised that we haven’t taken the time to thank you all for taking the demo for a spin! We were overwhelmed by your positive reception (242 reviews on the demo and 96% of them are positive!!!!). We’ve been spending the past few weeks going through your reviews & comments. Some of them made us chuckle, some of them touched us and a lot of them held very crucial feedback that we’ll be mulling over & implementing! 

So once again, thank you for playing, reviewing, sharing the game with your friends, and sharing your wildest theories. And, finally, thank you to press and influencers for the coverage!  We’ll get back to working on the final game (and a little surprise that we’ll keep to ourselves for a little bit longer). 

But before we leave you, we have…

 
One More Thing
You might’ve already seen it on our socials but: We’re incredibly excited to announce that we’ll be at Gamescom 2025, as part of the Indie Arena Booth! 

From August 20th to August 24th, you can check out our booth in Cologne and come chat with our friends at Iceberg Interactive about all things Strange. We will be pretty busy during the event but we'll try and be at the booth to meet people when we can. We’ll be sharing the exact details as we get closer to the convention. We’d love to put some faces behind your names.  

And who knows, maybe we’ll bring a goodie or two…  

See you in Cologne (or Undermere),

Rob & John

notes.title: Undermere Herald - May Edition | Meet Some Of Our Occult Locals
notes.content:
Dear reader,

Welcome to the May edition of the Undermere Herald - the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings. 

We don’t know what it is about Undermere, but something about our quaint little town attracts people seeking the thrill of the unknown. Some are adventurers, some are researchers - all have a hand in a world that few of us are familiar with. A world that lies behind dark curtains and buried in cold tombs.

In this month’s edition of the Herald, our reporters had a chat with some of our more esoteric inhabitants. You can read about their work, their connection to the occult… and maybe a sentence or two about the content of their character.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/c750532448234d9959ec6e29b59870d262e18185.png
Few in Undermere deserve the title ‘thrillseeker’ more than Barton Potter. A self-styled Relic Hunter, Potter has traversed the peaks of our hills and the depths of our catacombs, in search of the unusual and the arcane. He will gladly tell anyone who asks the story of how he lost the sight in his left eye, but it is never clear how much is true and how much is embellished to suit the ear of the listener.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/8431f38552e283c15f15933227b84fe5f79be7d2.png
Only the more unfortunate among you will be familiar with Dr. Francesca Robertson. She is not a doctor in the traditional sense… After a family tragedy, Dr. Robertson started looking for answers beyond the traditional textbooks, becoming one of the region’s foremost experts on occult maladies. When Noctic Sight invades your dreams or Morgan’s Insanity threatens to unpick your hold on reality, Dr. Robertson is the person you most want on your side.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/dfc8e539302dfb67d737272cafc8e1015e426a27.png
To say that Undermere would look very different without Verona Green would be an understatement. The Occult Scholar is an esteemed member of our community. Kind and humble, yes, but sharp of mind and not someone to underestimate. It is hard to imagine a more fitting figurehead for our town, but she would never accept a position of governance.

These are but a handful of our most arcanely attuned townsfolk. As we delve deeper into the mysteries that surround us, we invite you to reflect on the unseen threads that may connect you to the world behind the veil. We’d be curious to read about your connection to the occult in a reader’s letter!

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

notes.title: Undermere Herald - March Edition | Literary Inspirations & A Guessing Game
notes.content:
Dear reader,

Welcome to the March edition of the Undermere Herald - the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings.

Since you’re holding this physical newspaper in your hand right now, we’ll assume that you, just like the writing staff here at the Herald, are an avid reader! From the rich tomes of Dickens to the pastoral poems of Wordsworth & Coleridge, the literary arts are a rich well of creative inspiration. This month, we’ll discuss the works that inspire us.

Strange Antiquities’ (Literary) Inspirations

It’s hard to pinpoint specific inspirations for the world of Undermere because we’ve drawn from such a wide range of our interests, and there’s no one clear ‘main’ influence, but we’re going to try and break down some of those inspirations here.

Clearly, there is a Lovecraftian angle, but, like many modern Lovecraft-inspired works, it’s more of a distilled inspiration. Perhaps the main influence here is a board game called Eldritch Horror in which players battle against fearsome entities from other dimensions. The general ‘feel’ of the world, from the story vignettes when you visit locations, to the Dread/Sanity system, certainly takes inspiration from that game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/1743c0377fcdf10345abdd4a336f069b776087a1.jpg
Other smaller inspirations include Granny Weatherwax from Terry Pratchett's Discworld novels who is channeled through the no-nonsense Verona Green. And then there are the green-eyed Draer who are a nod to the blue-eyed Fremen from Frank Herbert's sci-fi epic, Dune.

Keen-eyed observers with a bit of local knowledge will also be able to spot several Lake District-based references, whether that be from local lore such as the witch Long Meg or the skulls of Calgarth Hall, or in the names of people and places, such as Barton Potter, Wainwright Hospital, and Naylor Island.

Can You Guess The Item? 

Before we let you go, readers, here’s a little challenge: Strange Antiquities is all about occult artefacts. Here are just a handful of the carefully designed items from the game. One of these is a Shadow Hold, which any Thaumaturge could tell you is for drawing out the manifestation known as Creeping Dark, but can you guess which one?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/04ab57a5f3aa4196e7927d777c9b2ee27de70332.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/308ed3f1f57d363d52d31f4bb5c0f006419cf754.png
And can you guess what any of the other items might be used for or what they might be called? You'll have to wait until the game comes out to find out if your guesses were correct!

notes.title: Undermere Herald - January Edition | A Brand-New Town Map
notes.content:
Dear readers,

Welcome to this year’s very first edition of the Undermere Herald – the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings.

And that’s exactly what our industrious writers will be focussing on this month! The key to not getting lost in the narrow and winding lanes of our beautiful town is a good & accurate map. 

Picture this: 

 You are visiting Undermere for the first time and, in an attempt to see the sights, you want to venture from the History Museum to the Pier to pay a visit to the Bleak Stones on Naylor Island. 
Or, maybe you’re a resident and you just uncovered a mysterious object in your attic that you’d like to get appraised at Strange Antiquities. 
Well, fret not! The local council of Undermere has just released a brand-new town map, listing all key locations in the town – including landmarks, public buildings, and businesses. Unlike the council’s previous maps, this one exclusively focuses on the town of Undermere rather than the surrounding area!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/085bdea105b841f5c4831d5025ef721ead1ad455.png

The Undermere Town Map is a great addition to anyone’s map collection, making interacting with the town easier for residents and visitors alike. 

Finally, you will be able to explore every inch of Undermere and discover your own story, without the fear of getting lost in its charming labyrinth of streets. If maps are your thing, then stay tuned - we've got more than just a town map hidden up our sleeves!

The Undermere Town Map is available for free at various locations throughout the town.

notes.title: A First Look at Strange Antiquities’ Refined Gameplay!

Dear Thaumaturges,

Remember that teaser from a while ago?

Well, today we’re incredibly excited to finally give you a more detailed glimpse into the wonderful world of Strange Antiquities. A few weeks ago, we got together in an old candle-lit cottage and tried to recreate some of the atmosphere from the game – rustic shelves, old maps, and as many strange-looking antiques as we could find – to film an exclusive, first look trailer! 

[previewyoutube=5YravLrvr6o;full][/previewyoutube]

In this gameplay trailer, you’ll get a first in-depth look at some of the mechanics in Strange Antiquities. We’ll take you through the updated Closer Inspect system that allows you to examine items in more detail, as well as the Thaumaturge's library of esoteric tomes.

For this sequel, we wanted to take the identity of Strange Horticulture, while building on the parts we all love and bringing more depth to the gameplay and detective work. It’ll still feel like Undermere with its cosy rain-soaked atmosphere and darkly mysterious undercurrent – but with new challenges, new puzzles, and new approaches. What new feature are you most excited about?

We can’t wait to show you more in the future,

John & Rob

notes.title: Undermere Herald - Special Edition | Revealing the Winners of our Art Contest!
notes.content:
Dear readers, 

Welcome to another special edition of the Undermere Herald - the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings.

As wintry winds sweep the streets and the frost settles on the windows of Undermere, what better time to sit down by the hearth and enjoy some beautiful art? That’s right, readers: after rigorous inspection and deliberation, we have chosen the winners of the Undermere Herald Art Contest.

Back in September, we challenged our most artistically inclined readers to design their version of the exterior of Undermere’s esteemed supplier of artefacts, Strange Antiquities, and quite frankly, we’re overwhelmed. We’re overwhelmed with the tremendous amount of art that has been sent in and it felt like an insurmountable task to determine a winner.

Before we dive into the outcome, we want to thank everyone who participated for their contributions! Seeing everyone’s art pour in has been inspiring, and the stunning artistry of your submissions took us aback, in the best possible way. 

Every single entry was unique & special, which is why we want you to see all of them. Hence why in a supplement to the Herald, we have shared what we loved about each piece.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

But without further ado, here are our winning entries in the Undermere Herald Art Contest. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/fe1e23669fba8cc042cca09c3937bba58fb0cdeb.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/8c30e8ae49bbe3385663ae5d6631cc704e1538bf.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/6075d5400260943b83fdf91303129c6daaf9ec27.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/8fbb123fa4f1a6acb22bbb23b69cd3b01e3495c4.jpg
As you can see we couldn't separate our two winners so we have given two first prizes! 

All our podium winners will get a Steam code for the game as soon as it releases. Our 2 winners also get some exclusive physical art prints which we will be in contact to arrange.

notes.title: Undermere Herald - November Edition | Art Contest Prize & Labels
notes.content:
Dear readers,

Welcome to the November edition of the Undermere Herald – the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings.

A shop like Strange Antiquities, with all its potentially dangerous, magical items, needs to be run like a tight ship. Thaumaturge Eli White ensures that none of his artefacts get in the hands of the wrong person through an intricate process of research and identification. But how does one keep track of the properties of such a vast array of items? The answer is simple: labels! 

The Labelling System

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/a5ee774a988d6d50d1ac52b004b5b6c396337055.png
Horticulturists among you know the importance of colourful labels and thoroughly enjoy labelling each new discovery you make. Strange Antiquities makes use of a more in-depth labelling system. Along with the options to pick different colours for each label, there are a variety of shapes to try out, and symbols that you can add to help put your own touch on the labels you give to your items.

We also know that some of you did not enjoy labelling plants so don't worry, we've got you covered too! Auto-labelling is still an option.

A Small Reminder

We would also like to remind the artists, scribes, tinkerers, etc., among you that submissions for the Undermere Herald’s art contest are still open and we’re finally ready to announce the prize!

As announced in the last edition, we’re looking for creative minds to imagine their own version of Strange Antiquities’ storefront. The winner of the contest will get an exclusive Strange Antiquities art print, created by John & Rob Donkin, the developers of the Strange series.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/8c04a3e6cb31f4b7b0c8a6bb3cd98d5a2ad5f106.jpg
To enter, you’ll have to show us the full scope of your creativity! Use any medium you choose—paint, clay, crochet, anything—to depict the exterior of Strange Antiquities. Let your ideas run wild, but keep it crafted by hand—no AI allowed. Submit your work via correspondence at contest@badviking.com by November 15th. 

We’ve been enamoured by the submissions so far and we can’t wait to see the rest!

notes.title: Undermere Herald - August Edition | Jupiter & Puzzle Design
notes.content:
Dear reader,

Welcome to the August edition of the Undermere Herald - the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings. 

As we’re nearing the end of the dog days of summer, it’s time to accustom ourselves to the coming of muckier weather. In today’s edition of the Herald, we’ll familiarise ourselves with one of Undermere’s most famous felines, while peeking behind the curtain of the shop he resides in — Strange Antiquities!

Jupiter

Jupiter is the Thaumaturge's cat. Or, perhaps more accurately, Eli is Jupiter's Thaumaturge. Jupiter found Strange Antiquities, perhaps drawn by the curiosities within, and made it his home. Eli was more than happy to accommodate him, but he learned early on that Jupiter was his own master.

His business is his own, but it largely consists of regular naps, terrorising rodents, and midnight explorations of Undermere and beyond. What he does on his excursions is a mystery, but he seems to be well-known among the residents of Undermere.

We named Jupiter after a lengthy brainstorming discussion where we explored the game’s themes to find something appropriate. We liked Jupiter because, as well as being associated with both astrology and alchemy, it is also the name of the cat in Robin Jarvis' excellent Deptford Mice series of books which we enjoyed as kids.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/afbff8cd536441e2c5be2654f13024f14bc12c20.png
Image 1: Jupiter – king of naps and death of rats

A Short Discussion on Puzzles

Those of you who have played Strange Horticulture will find the gameplay of Strange Antiquities familiar. The core of the game involves serving customers by using your detective skills to identify an item on your shelves. If you’re thinking, ‘but plants all have similar visual properties whereas items all look quite different so surely they’ll be easy to tell apart,’ you’d be absolutely right! This has been one of the main challenges we’ve faced while developing the game, but we find that these sorts of constraints can push us to be more creative and we’ve been able to take that central gameplay concept a lot further than we did in Strange Horticulture.

That means as a player you might expect to need to do a little more detective work this time around, perhaps flicking through your well-worn copy of Hermetic Symbology to track down a relevant symbol, or cross-referencing with a book on gemstones to learn which Thaumic discipline Bloodstone belongs to. We’ve still got some tweaking to do to make sure the difficulty is where we want it to be, but we’re excited for you to get your hands on it and find out what you make of it!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/6dc0e212ddf0cb3cee01a82f4c2a935e05589599.png
Image 2. An excerpt from 'Gemstones and their Thaumic Properties'

Strange Words

What better way to celebrate the investigative work of the Thaumaturge, than with a little brain teaser? See if you can find all the words in the very first Undermere Herald crossword puzzle! (Feel free to print it out or just solve it by clicking on the image!)

notes.title: Undermere Herald - July Edition | The Pitt Rivers museum and The Thaumaturge!
notes.content:
Dear reader,

Welcome to the inaugural edition of the Undermere Herald - the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings. In today’s edition, we will delve into the archaeological offerings of the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and introduce one of the town’s most sought-after tradespeople: the Thaumaturge, Eli White. 

Visiting the Pitt Rivers Museum:

As John and I live in different parts of the UK, it's sometimes a challenge to get together for anything work-related. The item designs have been one of the biggest challenges for us on Strange Antiquities, so we felt there was a good opportunity for us to get out of the office and go for a field trip! 

We’re lucky enough to live within a couple of hours of some excellent museums, including everything that London has to offer, so we were spoiled for choice, but the one that excited us the most was Oxford’s unique Pitt Rivers museum. It has an amazing collection of trinkets, curiosities, and artefacts from all over the world, all piled high in glass cabinets with handwritten labels, and mostly all in one big room. It’s very Strange Antiquities.

Going to Oxford also meant that we got two museums for the price of one – the Ashmolean is just down the road from the Pitt Rivers and is equally stuffed full of treasures. We had a great trip and came back buzzing with inspiration.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/1a3fbdcd4b28d62510504218a4eed2225e46e339.jpg
Image 1. A silvered, stoppered bottle said to contain a witch.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/397e94a6aed674921b888c339bd10d7fb087c2d0.jpg
                          Image 2. The stacked cabinets of the Pitt Rivers⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

Meet the Shopkeeper:

Unlike in Strange Horticulture, you are not the owner of the shop in Strange Antiquities. That role belongs to Eli White, local Thaumaturge and collector of Objects. Objects that to the untrained eye may appear dull and lifeless, but that in the right hands, and armed with the right knowledge, can be a gateway to so much more. For Eli, the quest to unearth and understand each new Object has been the driving force of his adult life.

As his apprentice you still have a lot to learn, but when Eli is called away to help with an important matter, he reluctantly leaves you in charge. He is a stern master who knows first-hand what can happen if the right precautions are not taken. He doesn’t tend to show much emotion, but he does have a more tender side – a side that is mostly reserved for the store’s cat, Jupiter.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/e7c23db0b9631833318b0c18929bdcb1b31fe50c.png
Image 3. Eli White – the Thaumaturge

notes.title: About my Name... meet Jupiter!
notes.content:
Dear Thaumaturges,


Over the past few days, we gave you a little mystery to solve. From celestial conundrums, over authorial anagrams, to planetary puzzles, we’ve had you guessing and theorising over something that we know is very dear to your hearts: the name of Strange Antiquities’ store cat. 

Reading everybody’s guesses was a delight! Some of you got very close; others less so. (Unfortunately, the cat’s name will not be Jon Bon Jovi). 

But without further ado, let’s get to the most important part of this blog…

Meet Jupiter!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/9fb0312671f7b1a7217e1c1eb359e146805323f4.png

Thanks to all who played along, and congratulations to everyone who guessed correctly – especially those of you who managed it after only one clue (we were stunned)!

Here’s a quick explanation of all the clues in case there are some you missed:
[olist]
 The holes are a representation of the planets (yes, including Pluto!)

 Sir Jon Vibar is an anagram of Robin Jarvis, author of a book called The Alchymist’s Cat. The titular cat is called Jupiter which is partly where the inspiration for our cat’s name came from!

 This is the symbol for the planetary metal, tin, which is associated with Jupiter.
[/olist]
Rob & John

notes.title: Strange things are happening in Undermere…
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/6427c433406768a58e06989056775d8c6aa4df9c.gif

Taking place several years after the events of Strange Horticulture, Strange Antiquities is a new, dark, and cosy standalone adventure set in the world of Undermere. It is a place of ancient woodland, candle-lit libraries, and macabre folklore, where strange things happen as often as it rains.

You are the Thaumaturge’s apprentice, tasked with running a shop dealing in occult antiquities. When hundreds of ravens start circling over the town of Undermere, those in the know become concerned. Occult Scholar Verona Green visits Strange Antiquities to enquire about the unnatural series of events. But before she is able to meet with the Thaumaturge, events take a sinister turn…

Check out the teaser trailer for a sneak peek of what awaits:
[previewyoutube=Ma1lDaPi82U;full][/previewyoutube]

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/157ba460d5c18c5930f7fd665d41ea747a843137.png
We are two brothers from the UK who have been making games together for over a decade. In 2022 we released our occult puzzle game Strange Horticulture, and the response has been incredible; from amazing reviews and award nominations to appearing in numerous best-of-the-year lists. Most importantly, it has been a joy to read the kind words left by so many of our players on Steam, where we are still rated Overwhelmingly Positive after almost 10,000 reviews!

We want to thank everyone who has played Strange Horticulture, left us a review, told their friends, or supported the game in any way. It has been an amazing journey and we can't wait to share the next chapter with you.

Please wishlist and follow Strange Antiquities here to stay up-to-date with the development and help us spread the word.

Many thanks,
Rob & John
